THE PAMPERED CHEF®
Smothered Chicken with Garlic
3 tbsp (45 mL) fresh rosemary or 1 tbsp (15 mL) dried rosemary, divided
½ tsp (2 mL) paprika
½ tsp (2 mL) salt
¼ tsp (1 mL) ground black pepper
1 whole chicken (about 4 lb/1.8 kg)
1 lemon, cut into quarters
1 tbsp (15 mL) olive oil
2 heads garlic, peeled (about 40 cloves)

p2:
Smothered Chicken with Garlic
1. Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C). Lightly spray Deep Covered Baker with oil. Combine half of the rosemary with paprika, salt and black pepper in small bowl; set aside. Remove and discard giblets and neck from chicken cavity. Rinse chicken with cold water; pat dry with paper towels. Trim excess fat, if necessary. Place lemon quarters and remaining rosemary inside cavity of chicken. Tie ends of legs together with cotton string. Lift wing tips up toward neck, then tuck under back of chicken. Place chicken breast side up into baker.
2. Brush outside of chicken with oil; coat completely with seasoning mixture. Arrange garlic around chicken. Bake, covered, 60 minutes. Carefully remove lid and continue roasting 25-35 minutes or until Pocket Thermometer registers 180°F (82°C) in thickest part of thigh and juices run clear. Remove chicken from baker; let stand 10 minutes before carving. Remove garlic from drippings; serve with chicken.
Yield: 4-6 servings

3/4 cup milk
1/3 cup butter or shortening
1 egg

By Elaine Young
   Nationally, Girl Scout Cookies have become somewhat of an institution. The sale varies from council to council, although in most cases, cookies are the major source of Girl Scout income.
   Locally, it has been a long association starting in 1936 with the first nationally sanctioned sale. However, Girl Scouts had been selling cookies several years prior to sanctioning.
   The earliest cookie sales represented a resourceful approach to insuring the financial stability of the movement. In those days, girls baked and packaged the cookies themselves. The following recipe was used:

1 cup butter              2 cups flour
2 cup sugar               2 teaspoons baking powder
2 eggs beaten             1/2 teaspoons salt
2 tablespoons milk        1 teaspoons vanilla

Cream butter and sugar. Add eggs, milk, vanilla and flour with salt and baking powder. Mix well. Chill about an hour. Roll very thin and cut out about the size of a baking powder lid. Bake at 425 degrees for 8 to 10 minutes. Sprinkle baked cookies with sugar.

FRESH MONK FISH

TO BAKE: Preheat oven to 350°. Butter shallow baking dish, arrange monk fish fillets. Sprinkle with salt and pepper; brush with melted butter. Bake 20-30 minutes, basting occasionally, until fish flakes easily when tested with fork.
TO POACH: Bring 2 cups water or milk to boil, add monk fish fillets. Cover; simmer 10 minutes, until fish flakes easily when tested with fork. Carefully remove from broth. Serve hot with lemon-butter sauce or cool in refrigerator; flake and use in salads, casseroles, or other dishes.
QUICK TOUCHES: Use poached monk fish in any of your favorite lobster recipes. Here's a quick way to fix monk fish thermidor. In sauce pan, cook 1/2 cup onions in 2 tablespoons butter until tender. Add 1 can condensed cream of mushroom soup, 1/4 cup sour cream, and 2 pounds poached monk fish fillets cut in cubes. Heat, stirring occasionally.
